column3: “Was old and satisfied with days” is rendered “reached old age”; the phrase “satisfied with days” is not rendered separately.
The Hebrew “which I made” is rendered “which David made.”
NASB reads “Shelomoth,” the spelling read aloud, for the written “Shelomith.” “Heads of the fathers” is rendered “heads of the fathers' households.”
“The chief” is rendered “the first,” and “a group” as “one class.”

“To consecrate it a holy one of holy ones” is rendered “to sanctify him as most holy”; the meaning is uncertain, as it can also mean consecrating the most holy things. “Make smoke” is rendered “burn incense,” and “descendants” as “sons.”
“Descendants” is rendered “sons,” and “named on the tribe” as “named among the tribe.”
“Sons” is rendered “son,” and “numerous upward” as “very many.”
“To their enrolled ones” is rendered “of those of them who were counted”; “to their skulls” is rendered “by their census.”
“There is not to carry” is rendered “will no longer need to carry,” and “articles” as “utensils.”
“Function” is rendered “office,” “to the side of” as “to assist,” and “store-rooms” as “chambers.”
“The bread of the row” is rendered “the showbread”; “every measurement and measurement” is rendered “all measures of volume and size.”
“In the morning in the morning” is rendered “every morning.”
